
```{devoirs_choices conversion_factor_3_two_choices}
- A dimensionless ratio of equal quantities used to convert between commensurate units.:
    correct: true
    feedback: Correct.
- Dimensions formed by multiplying or dividing base dimensions.:
    correct: false
    feedback: This describes derived dimensions, not conversion factor. In this chapter,
      conversion factor refers to a dimensionless ratio of equal quantities used to
      convert between commensurate units.
- Dimensionless ratios formed by dividing two exactly equal quantities.:
    correct: false
    feedback: This describes flavors of one, not conversion factor. In this chapter,
      conversion factor refers to a dimensionless ratio of equal quantities used to
      convert between commensurate units.
- A one-dimensional line on which points represent values of a quantity.:
    correct: false
    feedback: This describes number line, not conversion factor. In this chapter,
      conversion factor refers to a dimensionless ratio of equal quantities used to
      convert between commensurate units.
- A multiplier such as meters per mile that cancels the starting unit and leaves the target unit.:
    correct: true
    feedback: Correct.
```
